investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable for 130–147 seconds. The Kubernetes scheduler reported that only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to help.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote-agent pods. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption finding no victims, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable indefinitely. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1764) never returns a VM identity or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 251–256 cannot be satisfied. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource fully consumed on both eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', meaning the resource quota is at zero on both peerpods-capable nodes. No new remote-agent pod can be admitted until existing consumers release the resource or node capacity is expanded.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the scheduler reports '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', meaning those nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods regardless of available resources. A misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could be reducing the effective scheduling pool.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations: if prior eval runs or user-created agents did not clean up their pods, those allocations would persist and exhaust the resource for new pods. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1762) but cleanup may not have completed if a prior run was interrupted.

Lower confidence — recent change 978e0a1 'ci(evals): speed up functional smoke setup' touched all three eval infrastructure files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs); it is possible this change altered agent creation parameters or concurrency in a way that increased pod demand, but no source diff is available to confirm this hypothesis.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-18 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure localized to the Kubernetes swarm node pool backing remote agent VM provisioning; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. This prevented the eval runner from completing createAgent (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1784), so the probe timed out after ~146–149 seconds and returned a failure message instead of the required evidence fields. The same scheduler exhaustion simultaneously blocked remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime, confirming the failure is at the shared VM-provisioning layer rather than in any single eval branch.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable for 130–147 seconds. The Kubernetes scheduler reported that only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to help.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote-agent pods. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption finding no victims, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable indefinitely. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1764) never returns a VM identity or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 251–256 cannot be satisfied. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource fully consumed on both eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', meaning the resource quota is at zero on both peerpods-capable nodes. No new remote-agent pod can be admitted until existing consumers release the resource or node capacity is expanded.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the scheduler reports '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', meaning those nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods regardless of available resources. A misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could be reducing the effective scheduling pool.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations: if prior eval runs or user-created agents did not clean up their pods, those allocations would persist and exhaust the resource for new pods. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1762) but cleanup may not have completed if a prior run was interrupted.

Lower confidence — recent change 978e0a1 'ci(evals): speed up functional smoke setup' touched all three eval infrastructure files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs); it is possible this change altered agent creation parameters or concurrency in a way that increased pod demand, but no source diff is available to confirm this hypothesis.

If the pod spec for remote agent creation does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would indicate a different underlying misconfiguration rather than true capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime passed in a concurrent run, the failure would be localized to the state-polling logic rather than the shared VM provisioning layer.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries Kubernetes node capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested slots and fails fast when headroom drops below a configured threshold, rather than waiting for a pod scheduling timeout.
Add a kata.peerpods.io/vm pool saturation warning check that fires before the outage threshold is reached, giving operators time to act before all remote-agent checks fail.

Add a historical pass/fail baseline for the remote-agents feature so that regressions from a passing state are immediately flagged; the current verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, meaning no baseline exists.
Consider a canary eval that provisions a single remote agent VM at low frequency to detect capacity exhaustion before the full eval suite runs, reducing the blast radius of a saturated pool.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the agent VM never became schedulable and the runtime probe never reached the point of returning orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–149 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent runtime was never reached, and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) received zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1797: createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) is the call that submits the remote pod; scheduling failure here blocks all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, confirming the runtime check is a non-required signal but still failed for the same underlying reason.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This directly matches the scheduler message in failed-check.message and all three sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are at VM capacity. If the affinity rules were broadened or additional matching nodes were added, scheduling might succeed.

Tertiary — a burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads (from other users, CI jobs, or a previous eval run) consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before the eval pods were submitted, leaving no room for preemption victims.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages explicitly names Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm as the blocking condition on the 2 affinity-matching nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes and amplifying the VM resource exhaustion impact.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe
affectedAreas.reason: The probe at line 1797 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which submits the pod that fails to schedule. All downstream evidence collection (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is blocked by this failure.

affectedAreas.label: Eval expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: Contract at line 263–266 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura'. None of these were collectible because the pod never started.

affectedAreas.label: Feature registry — remote-agents feature (degradedAfterFailures: 1)
affectedAreas.reason: With degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, and both required checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failing, the feature health signal will reflect degraded or outage status in the eval dashboard.

recommendedNextActions: Investigate current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the two affinity-matching nodes to determine whether exhaustion is persistent or was a transient spike at the time of the eval run (2026-06-18T15:46–15:51Z).
Identify and, if appropriate, terminate any leaked or long-running pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the affinity-matching nodes to restore scheduling capacity.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods: if only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible, consider whether additional nodes can be labeled to match, reducing the blast radius of per-node VM exhaustion.

Add a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent eval probes that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting pod creation, so scheduling failures produce a more actionable SKIP or WARN status rather than a timeout-driven FAIL.
Consider adding a cluster-level alert on kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization approaching 100% on affinity-matching nodes so capacity exhaustion is detected before it causes eval failures.

recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node for each node that matches the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector and check the Allocatable and Requests fields for kata.peerpods.io/vm.

recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Use kubectl get pods --all-namespaces with a field selector or resource filter to enumerate pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two relevant nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that once capacity is available the pod schedules, the agent runtime responds, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are collected.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 4-node affinity mismatch is intentional or whether the selector could be broadened to distribute scheduling pressure.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec submitted by createAgent for type 'remote' and verify which node labels or taints are required, and how many cluster nodes satisfy them.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the next eval run and pods still fail to schedule, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but a different scheduling constraint.

If the two affinity-matching nodes show zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable (i.e., the resource is not configured or the device plugin is not running), the cause is a missing or misconfigured device plugin rather than slot exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and collects all required evidence, it would indicate a transient capacity spike rather than a persistent exhaustion condition.
If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm and the scheduler message is produced by a different mechanism, the diagnosis would need to be revised.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all remote-agent-eligible nodes, failing with a capacity warning before pod submission is attempted.
Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 healthy, schedulable nodes with available VM slots).
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent eval pods are left running after a probe cycle completes, catching leaked pods that would exhaust VM slots for subsequent runs.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerMessage, unschedulableReason) so future failures are immediately diagnosable without manual kubectl inspection.
